question: A student had 14 items initially. They added 80 more through collection. They added 6 from trades. They multiplied by 3 for display. They removed 266 for storage. They added 66 back for show. The school had 500 students. How many items displayed?

A runner had 99 miles initially. They multiplied by 7 through training. They divided by 3 for weekly splits. They multiplied by 8 for distance. They added 63 bonus miles. Converting to minutes per hour shows pace. How many distance miles?

A construction crew had 208 supplies. They multiplied by 6 for project needs. They divided by 3 for team distribution. They multiplied by 5 for final allocation. They added 7 more items. The workday lasted 8 hours. How many items allocated?

A restaurant started with 221 meals Monday. They added 17 more Tuesday morning. They multiplied by 5 through the week. They added 42 from prep Wednesday. They removed 797 for a large event. They added 4 from last-minute orders. They added 6 from donations. The kitchen had 10 staff. How many meals available?

A warehouse had 90 boxes initially. They removed 86 damaged boxes. They multiplied by 6 for restocking. They removed 8 for urgent orders. They added 58 from suppliers. They multiplied by 7 for shipping. The facility had 20 workers. How many boxes for shipping?

A farm had 137 animals initially. They removed 56 sold to market. They multiplied by 7 for breeding count. They added 68 newborns. They multiplied by 8 for total stock. Converting to pairs of animals. How many total animals?

A factory produced 76 items Monday. They multiplied by 8 Tuesday. They multiplied by 7 Wednesday. They added 77 Thursday items. They multiplied by 2 for Friday expansion. They multiplied by 8 for weekend prep. They added 4 from quality control. The facility had 50 employees. How many items total?

A warehouse received 180 boxes Monday. They added 3 Tuesday. They divided by 3 for sections. They added 66 Wednesday. They multiplied by 9 for export. The facility exported 100 items daily. How many export units?

A business had 192 items Monday morning. They added 51 Tuesday. They added 56 Wednesday. They added 67 Thursday. They removed 122 for distribution. The company had 8 departments. How many items distributed?

A collector had 155 items initially. They multiplied by 6 for collection value. They multiplied by 8 for display sets. They multiplied by 9 for categories. They removed 1344 for storage. The collection took years to build. How many categories removed?

A restaurant had 208 meals initially. They added 49 from prep. They multiplied by 3 for service hours. They multiplied by 6 for locations. They added 67 bonus meals. The kitchen operated 24 hours. How many served meals?

A student had 93 coins initially. They added 74 more. They added 36 from parents. They removed 63 for purchases. They removed 14 for charity. The student attended school 5 days weekly. How many coins remaining?

A farm had 176 items initially. They added 26 more supplies. They removed 10 damaged items. They divided by 3 for distribution. They multiplied by 5 for different uses. They added 36 from new purchases. They multiplied by 9 for final inventory. The farm had 50 acres. How many inventory items?

A student had 18 coins initially. They added 47 from allowance. They removed 49 for shopping. They added 24 from a gift. They removed 26 for savings. The school bank had 1000 accounts. How many coins left?

A contractor had 32 tools initially. He multiplied by 6 for project needs. He added 29 from storage. He removed 192 lost items. He removed 22 broken tools. He removed 2 more damaged. Converting to hourly rental shows cost. How many tools operational?

A warehouse had 223 boxes initially. They removed 108 for shipping. They multiplied by 3 for storage organization. They multiplied by 6 for distribution. They removed 1393 for a large order. They removed 277 damaged boxes. The facility employed 40 people. How many boxes remaining?

A student had 32 items initially. They removed 21 for a project. They removed 7 for trading. They added 65 from purchases. They multiplied by 4 for display. They added 58 from gifts. Converting to dozens shows storage. How many display items?

A baker had 12 pastries initially. They multiplied by 2 for morning baking. They added 27 from the oven. They added 50 from afternoon baking. They multiplied by 4 for delivery routes. They removed 173 for sales. Converting to dozens shows daily bakes. How many total pastries?

In the morning, James had 112 dollars. By midday, his income increased 7 times. In the afternoon, he spent 291 dollars on supplies. By evening, he had to pay another 360 dollars in expenses. His remaining funds were then multiplied by 5. Finally, his account balance tripled. How much money does James have now? His friend David had 400 dollars.

A bakery started with 215 kilograms of flour. In the morning, they received 24 kilograms more. By midday, they had used 130 kilograms for bread. In the afternoon, they got 51 kilograms from a supplier. Then they purchased 49 kilograms. By evening, they bought 78 kilograms. How many kilograms of flour does the bakery have at the end of the day?

Sarah started with 159 cents in savings. She spent 83 cents at the market. Her remaining money grew by a factor of 9 due to interest. She earned 80 more cents. Her total then increased 7 times. Finally, she earned 40 cents. Tom had 5000 cents in his account. How many total cents does Sarah have? Converting to dollars, her total is worth how much?

Rachel had 228 books in her collection. She multiplied her collection 5 times through new purchases. She then received 29 more books as gifts. She donated 609 books to a charity. Finally, she found 7 forgotten books in storage. How many books does Rachel have now? Her friend Lisa has 400 books.

A library had 163 books on its main shelf. During the morning, 23 books were returned. By afternoon, 39 more books were returned. Then, 201 books were removed for repair. The remaining books were reduced to a third. Finally, 26 new books were added. The library received a donation of 50 books. How many books does the library have at the end?

In the morning, Sam had 119 dollars. By midday, he spent 103 dollars. In the afternoon, he spent 9 more dollars. By evening, his remaining money doubled. Later, his money increased 5 times. As night fell, it increased another 9 times. How much money does Sam have by the end of the day?

A bakery started with 13 cookies. Production doubled in the morning. It tripled by midday. It multiplied 4 times by afternoon. The total cookies were divided equally among 6 retail stores. How many cookies does each store receive?
